unresolvedReferences.description: The treatise dates the emperor’s abdication to a fifth year after Jingyuan 1; Jingyuan has no canonical year 5, so the Western year is taken as AD 264 by ordinal count and remains internally loose.
The Three Princes (三王) who rose against Prince Zhao Lun are a collective and are not individuated.
Usurpation is also placed in the year after Tai’an 2, which conflicts with the Yongkang 1–next-year (AD 301) dating in s0230.
The 帝 who died in Guangxi 1/11 is identified only as Emperor Huai’s predecessor; no personal name is given in this chunk.
太后 is individuated but unnamed; her personal identity is not given in this chunk.
The 天子 held at Stone Fortress after Ming’s death is the reigning emperor of that revolt; the chunk does not supply his personal or temple name.
The female ruler holding court is not identified with a personal name; she is recorded as a separate local person from Empress Dowager Chu.
The interior governor of Kuaiji slain by Sun En is unnamed.
The interior governors slain in Sun En’s fifth-year raids are unnamed.
甘氏 is cited without an independent life date; chronology for Gan remains a research hold.
Sun Xiu’s defection is dated only 二年 after the Taishi 4 omen, without a restated era, so the Western year remains unresolved.
Zhang and Pei are named only by surname; the chapter does not further identify them.
